status_effects.explanation: He is locally elevated by being singled out, alongside the duchess, as one of the two most elegant people in Paris, though the claim's shallow basis is treated with narratorial irony.

appraisal_events.evidence: « Bébel, disait-elle, prétend que nous sommes les deux personnes les plus élégantes de Paris, parce qu'il n'y a que moi et lui qui ne nous laissions pas saluer par Mme et Gilberte... » Et la duchesse riait de tout son coeur.
appraisal_events.explanation: Bréauté's boast that he and the duchess are the two most elegant people in Paris is recounted with evident delight by the duchess, pairing him with her as a joint arbiter of elegance; the narrator's broader ironic framing of this vain, exclusion-based notion of 'elegance' tempers the praise.
